question: Is my house eligible for solar panels?

confidence.text: High: the listing, conservation area and Article 4 records agree, and the roof reading is clean (11% trees or chimneys).

limitations: The share of solar power used at home follows the MCS tables for 3,100 kWh a year (you told us); your own pattern may differ.
Rules for England, demo data for London.
Roof size and yield come from 1 m LIDAR and PVGIS: an installer's survey confirms them.
solar.next_step: Get quotes from two or three MCS certified installers. If you want it in writing, apply to Camden for a lawful development certificate.

facts.value: Basements (A4Ba3, from 2016-10-03): Removes permitted development for basements across the whole borough. Planning data says made 3 Oct 2016; Camden says adopted 1 Jun 2017.
S, 2.9 kWp, about 2916 kWh a year
facts.source: PVGIS 5.2, EU Joint Research Centre via Zetaris; roof from EA LIDAR

rules.clause: GPDO Sch 2 Part 14 Class A, A.2(c)
rules.plain: On a pitched roof, panels may stand up to 20 cm proud of the roof and may not go above the ridge.

rules.clause: GPDO Sch 2 Part 14 Class A, A.2(e)
rules.plain: In a conservation area, panels may not go on a wall, balcony or roof enclosure that faces a road. The roof is fine.

usage.text: Your roof could make about 94% of the 3,100 kWh you use a year (you told us, 25 Oct 2026).

lines.one: Your south roof slope (27°) has room for about 2.9 kWp, about 2,916 kWh a year.
lines.why: This house is not listed and sits in Dartmouth Park Conservation Area (1992), where panels cannot go on a wall facing a road: your west wall faces Dartmouth Park Avenue and your south wall faces Laurier Road, and the south slope can take them. The Article 4 direction on file (basements, A4Ba3) does not cover solar panels.
lines.get: About 2.9 kWp on the south slope, about 2,916 kWh a year.
lines.cost: For 2.9 kWp: about £4,600 to £6,100 to install, worth about £280 to £540 a year for the 3,100 kWh a year you use, so about 9 to 22 years to pay back. No VAT on panels until 31 Mar 2027.

challenges: No Article 4 that touches energy upgrades is on record for this house. Councils publish unevenly, so that alone is not proof. Does Camden publish conservation area Article 4s at all?
One cost figure would hide how much prices vary. Check the national median against the London average before quoting a cost.
One share of solar power used at home would hide that it depends on who is home in the day. Ask the MCS tables for all three occupancy types, for this roof and the owner's yearly use.
